title: SLA-aware regional switchover and deprecation window for versioned model routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Scope: implement an SLA-aware regional switchover mechanism and deprecation window for version-pinned models. This ticket covers server-side routing logic, control-plane signals for deprecation windows, and operator tooling to preview and force switchover. The goal is to ensure customer traffic bound to a pinned model version can be routed to approved variants or regional fallbacks with deterministic SLO-preserving behavior while providing explicit deprecation signals and an automated warmup path for variant candidates.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Add a routing policy that evaluates (in order) region affinity, explicit variant weights, SLA budget, and deprecation windows to choose a runtime target.
- Provide a deprecation window metadata field (start_ts, soft_warn_duration, hard_cutover_ts) surfaced in the model catalog and the pin API.
- When a pinned variant is unhealthy or overloaded, automatically failover to an ordered list of variant candidates or a regional equivalent while honoring per-customer latency SLOs (latency and error-rate budget).
- Ensure deterministic decision logging for every routed request (routing_trace_id) for postmortem and billing reconciliation.
- Expose a console preview and a dry-run toggle in the API to simulate the switchover decision for an account without moving traffic.
- Rollout must include integration tests exercising cold-warm variant warmups, telemetry triggers, and operator-initiated aborts/rollbacks.

Design decisions and rationale:
- SLA budget-first ordering: prioritize routing decisions that preserve per-customer latency/error budgets rather than strict model variant preference. This reduces P99 regression risk for production customers.
- Deprecation windows: a two-phase window (soft warn -> hard cutover) gives customers time to accept the new baseline while allowing automated mitigation (graceful downgrade, traffic mirroring) in soft window.
- Warmup choreography: when routing to a lower-cost quantized variant, the system will pre-warm KV caches and issue a short token-limited verification workload to detect quality regressions before full traffic shift.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: per-region and per-customer thresholds guard against adoption loops (rapid oscillation). Threshold parameters are configurable and tied to account tier.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs. speed: making routing decision logic fully synchronous with the config catalog ensures correctness but adds latency. We chose a cached config with short TTL plus eventual consistency signals for control-plane updates to minimize per-request latency.
- Complexity vs. observability: richer routing (SLA-aware scoring) increases complexity; we invest in request-level routing traces and unit cost accounting to ensure debuggability.

Implementation plan:
1) Catalog changes: add deprecation fields and variant priority lists to model metadata (runtime-2.4 schema change).
2) Routing engine: implement SLA-aware scorer (latency_budget_score, error_budget_score, region_score, variant_compatibility) as pluggable modules.
3) Warmup service: reuse existing KV warmup job with a guarded verification step.
4) Control-plane API: pin update endpoints to include dry-run and preview modes.
5) Console: preview UI for switchover simulation and deprecation timeline visualization.
6) Tests and canary: unit tests, integration tests, and a staged canary on internal traffic then opt-in beta customers.

APIs and config changes to surface:
- model_catalog.update: add "deprecation_window" and "variant_candidates" fields.
- pin.modify: accept "slo_constraints" object and "dry_run" param.
- routing.trace: return tracing metadata attributes (routing_trace_id, selected_variant, score_breakdown).

Operational runbook (initial):
- Alert on increased rollback rate (>2 rollbacks/hour for a single account) and rising warmup failures.
- Manual abort endpoint: operator can toggle pin to "hold" state preventing auto-switchover.
- Automated rollback: when warmup verification fails X consecutive times or SLO budget is breached for >5m, automatically revert to last-known-good variant and notify owner.

Metrics to monitor:
- P50/P95/P99 latency for pinned-model traffic by variant and region.
- Warmup success rate and time-to-warm.
- Number of auto-failovers and operator aborts.
- Routing decisions per reason bucket (unhealthy, overload, deprecation_cutover, sla_violation).

Backward compatibility: default behavior for existing pins is preserved (no auto-switchover) unless customers opt-in by setting a deprecation window or enabling auto-fallback. Migration instructions included in the design doc.

Security: routing metadata contains only identifiers; no customer PII. Role-based controls added to prevent non-privileged users from forcing global cutovers.

Open questions:
- What are safe default circuit-breaker thresholds for free-tier vs enterprise? (action: PM to define initial defaults)
- Exact verification workload for warmup (size & prompt types) to represent quality metrics. (action: ML team to propose)

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/infra/pages/PM-50821-deprecation-routing
- Initial Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XXX/deprecation-preview
- Proof-of-concept PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8321

Acceptance tests (condensed):
- Simulate pinned model unavailability -> routing picks first regional candidate within SLO budget.
- Enable deprecation soft window -> console shows warnings and dry-run returns expected target variant but no traffic moved.
- Warmup fails on verification -> automatic rollback and operator alert triggered.

Deployment plan:
- Merge routing change behind feature flag.
- Canary on internal-account traffic (2 days) -> metrics check -> opt-in beta customers (1 week) -> general availability behind account-level opt-in (1 month).
